note.note:
Consult Summary:
- 26-year-old woman presents with a 3-day history of progressively worsening, severe headache focused around the right eye, associated with photophobia and visual disturbance, unresponsive to ibuprofen; clinical features and family history suggest possible new-onset migraine.

History:
- Presenting complaint: “Crazy” headache ongoing for approximately 3 days, mainly located around the right eye but also described as involving the entire head.
- Onset: Gradually began three days ago at work; headache increased in severity by end of day one.
- Duration: Constantly present (“always there”), but fluctuates in intensity.
- Progression: Worsening over past three days.
- Severity: Reported as 8/10 at worst.
- Nature: Mostly dull, occasionally becomes sharper.
- Exacerbating factors: None specifically identified; screen use due to work may contribute.
- Relieving factors: Ibuprofen (taken 3/day for 2 days) provided no relief this episode (previously effective).
- Associated symptoms:
  - Photophobia (hurts to look at bright lights)
  - Visual disturbance (described as “shooting lights” at onset)
  - Nausea (“feel sick with the headache”), but no vomiting
  - Difficulty focusing at work
  - No loss of vision, no speech disturbance, no limb weakness, no fever, no neck stiffness, no rash, no recent head injury
- Pertinent negatives: No prior personal history of migraines; no other major symptoms.

Past Medical History:
- No chronic medical conditions reported.
- No prior personal migraine history.
- Wears glasses since age 5; no recent eye examination.

Medications:
- Tried ibuprofen (3 tablets per day for past 2 days; dose/route/frequency not fully documented).
- No regular medications.
- Not using oral contraceptive pill.
- Allergies: None known.

Social History:
- Lives with three housemates.
- Works in IT, heavy computer use.
- Social smoker and social alcohol consumption.
- Describes mild work stress (starting a new project), but not markedly elevated.

Family History:
- Mother and sister have frequent migraines (mother’s migraines are severe, sister’s are rare).

Physical Examination:
- Vitals: Not recorded.
- Examination findings: Not recorded.

Investigations:
- No labs or imaging ordered or mentioned.

Assessment & Plan:

Overall Impression:
- New-onset, severe, right periorbital headache with photophobia and visual disturbance, unresponsive to usual analgesia, and strong family history of migraine. Features highly suggestive of migraine (possibly first episode).

DDx Integration (brief):
1. Migraine (without aura, possibly with some visual aura features): Supported by severe lateralized headache, photophobia, visual symptoms, nausea, difficulty concentrating, and strong family history; lack of prior personal migraine history and resistance to ibuprofen noted but not exclusionary.
2. Tension-type (or eye strain) headache: Possible due to computer work and bilateral/dull nature, but severity, photophobia, and visual symptoms are less typical; family history more suggestive of migraine.
3. Sinusitis: Location overlaps, but lacks nasal, fever, or facial tenderness; photophobia and “shooting lights” make this less likely.

Issue 1: Headache (Probable New-Onset Migraine)
- Assessment: Headache with migrainous features; no concerning red flags for secondary causes on this assessment.
- Plan:
  - Counselled on appropriate use and dosing of ibuprofen (up to two tablets three times daily if tolerated).
  - Offer prescription for stronger analgesia (options included naproxen, paracetamol, codeine; dosing not specified).
  - Consider adding paracetamol or codeine for breakthrough pain.
  - Recommendation to keep a headache diary to monitor frequency, triggers, and response to treatment.
  - Advised to schedule follow-up in 1–2 weeks to reassess or sooner if symptoms worsen.
  - Safety advice: Return urgently if develops vision changes, limb weakness, speech disturbance, or systemic illness.

Issue 2: Eye Health/Strain (Secondary Concern)
- Assessment: Longstanding use of glasses; no recent eye test; increased screen time at work.
- Plan:
  - Advised to consider an updated eye test if symptoms of eye strain persist.

Issue 3: Preventive Migraine Therapy (Future Consideration)
- Assessment: Option for prophylactic therapy discussed if headaches become recurrent or frequent.
- Plan:
  - To be considered at future follow-up if indicated.

General plan items:
- Encourage hydration and stress management as general headache prevention strategies.
- Advised to reduce screen brightness as tolerated.

Quality checks:
● Missing but clinically expected elements: No documented physical examination or vital signs; medication-dose/route/frequency not fully specified; allergy status confirmed.
● No transcript/DDx conflicts identified.
● Transcript quality: Good; history comprehensive. No significant inaudible/noisy sections.
